slides.text: Never put a Hook in an if 🚫
slides.say: Why can't you call a hook inside an if statement?
This breaks. React doesn't know hooks by name. It tracks them by the order they're called.

slides.text: If the order changes between renders, state gets mixed up.
slides.say: If a condition skips one hook, every hook after it gets the wrong state. Chaos.

slides.text: ✅ Call Hooks at the top level, every render, same order.
slides.say: So: call hooks at the top level, in the same order, on every render. Put the condition inside the hook's logic instead.
